# Codebase Exploration Report This is a **minimal Next.js App Router starter**, clearly set up as a fixture for building an admin-protected area. There is no pages router, no CSS framework, no existing admin routes, and `forbidden()`/`unauthorized()` are **not used yet**. --- ## 1. Project structure: App Router **App Router only.** No `pages/` directory. ``` /workspace ├── app/ │ ├── layout.tsx # Root layout │ ├── page.tsx # Home page │ └── lib/ │ └── auth.ts # Mock session/auth helpers ├── next.config.ts # Empty config ├── package.json ├── tsconfig.json # @/* path alias └── .gitignore ``` Missing (do not exist yet): - `app/admin/` - `app/forbidden.tsx` / `forbidden.js` - `app/unauthorized.tsx` / `unauthorized.js` - `app/not-found.tsx` - `app/error.tsx` / `global-error.tsx` - `middleware.ts` - Any CSS files - Tests, README Path alias: `@/*` → project root (`@/app/lib/auth`). --- ## 2. Authentication / sessions All auth lives in one mock module. **File:** `/workspace/app/lib/auth.ts` ```1:32:/workspace/app/lib/auth.ts // Mock authentication library // In a real app, this would verify session tokens, JWTs, etc. export interface Session { userId: string role: 'user' | 'admin' name: string } // Simulates getting the current user's session // Returns null if not authenticated export async function getSession(): Promise { // For testing purposes, return a non-admin user return { userId: '123', role: 'user', // Not an admin name: 'John Doe', } } // Helper to check if user has admin role export async function verifyAdmin(): Promise<{ isAdmin: boolean session: Session | null }> { const session = await getSession() return { isAdmin: session?.role === 'admin', session, } } ``` ### Session / role types | Type | Definition | |------|------------| | `Session` | `{ userId: string; role: 'user' \| 'admin'; name: string }` | | `getSession()` | `Promise` — currently **always** returns a logged-in **non-admin** user | | `verifyAdmin()` | `Promise<{ isAdmin: boolean; session: Session \| null }>` — `isAdmin` is `session?.role === 'admin'` | There is no cookie/JWT/middleware, no NextAuth, no Clerk. Roles are a string union: `'user' | 'admin'`. `getSession()` is hardcoded so any admin page that checks `verifyAdmin()` will fail for the current user. That is intentional for testing 403 behavior. --- ## 3. Existing page / layout patterns **Root layout** — `/workspace/app/layout.tsx` ```1:19:/workspace/app/layout.tsx import type { Metadata } from 'next' export const metadata: Metadata = { title: 'Admin Dashboard', description: 'Admin area with auth protection', } export default function RootLayout({ children, }: Readonly<{ children: React.ReactNode }>) { return ( {children} ) } ``` **Home page** — `/workspace/app/page.tsx` ```1:12:/workspace/app/page.tsx import Link from 'next/link' export default function Home() { return (

Welcome

This is the home page.

Go to Admin Dashboard
) } ``` UI conventions: - Server Components (no `'use client'`) - Semantic HTML: `
`, `

`, `

` - `next/link` for navigation - No CSS classes, no component library - Typed `Metadata` export - `Readonly<{ children: React.ReactNode }>` layout props No error pages, loading UI, or route groups exist. --- ## 4. Existing admin-related code There is **no admin route**. The home page links to `/admin`, which does not exist yet. Admin-related pieces today: - Metadata title/description mention “Admin Dashboard” / “auth protection” - Home link: `Go to Admin Dashboard` - `verifyAdmin()` helper in `app/lib/auth.ts` --- ## 5. Next.js version and `forbidden()` / `unauthorized()` **Next.js:** `^16.3.1-canary.15` **React:** `19.1.0` `forbidden()` and `unauthorized()` **are exported** from `next/navigation` in this version, but: - **Not used anywhere in app source** - They still check `experimental.authInterrupts` (`process.env.__NEXT_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTH_INTERRUPTS`) - `next.config.ts` is empty — **`experimental.authInterrupts` is not enabled** Calling `forbidden()` without enabling that flag will throw: > `` `forbidden()` is experimental and only allowed to be enabled when `experimental.authInterrupts` is enabled. `` File conventions supported by this Next version: - `forbidden.js` / `forbidden.tsx` → rendered on 403 - `unauthorized.js` / `unauthorized.tsx` → rendered on 401 - Default fallbacks exist in Next internals (`status={403}`, `"This page could not be accessed."`) --- ## 6. Styling approach **None.** No Tailwind, CSS Modules, styled-components, or global CSS. - No `.css` / `.module.css` files - No Tailwind / PostCSS / styled-jsx deps - Pages use unstyled semantic HTML Match that: keep new pages as plain JSX unless you add a stylesheet. --- ## 7. 403 / error page patterns **None exist.** No `forbidden.tsx`, `unauthorized.tsx`, `not-found.tsx`, `error.tsx`, or `global-error.tsx`. Next will use its built-in 403 fallback if `forbidden()` is called (after enabling `authInterrupts`). --- ## Recommended approach (match existing conventions) This repo is clearly meant for an **admin dashboard protected with `forbidden()`**. 1. **Enable auth interrupts** in `/workspace/next.config.ts`: ```ts import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const nextConfig: NextConfig = { experimental: { authInterrupts: true, }, } export default nextConfig ``` 2. **Add `app/admin/page.tsx`** as a Server Component (same style as home): - Call `verifyAdmin()` (or `getSession()`) - If `!isAdmin`, call `forbidden()` from `next/navigation` - If admin, render a simple `

` dashboard 3. **Optionally add `app/forbidden.tsx`** for a custom 403 UI, matching the home page pattern: ```tsx export default function Forbidden() { return (

403 – Forbidden

You do not have permission to access this page.

) } ``` 4. **Do not invent new auth.** Reuse `getSession` / `verifyAdmin` and the `Session` type from `@/app/lib/auth`. 5. **Use `unauthorized()` only if you treat “no session” separately from “not admin”.** Today `getSession()` always returns a user, so `forbidden()` (403, wrong role) is the correct primitive. `unauthorized()` is for 401 (not logged in). 6. **Keep styling as plain semantic HTML** (`
`, `

`, `

`, `Link`) to stay consistent. 7. Prefer **route-level check in the admin page or `app/admin/layout.tsx`**, not middleware — there is no middleware today, and `forbidden()` is designed for Server Components. **Role check pattern:** ```ts import { forbidden } from 'next/navigation' import { verifyAdmin } from '@/app/lib/auth' export default async function AdminPage() { const { isAdmin, session } = await verifyAdmin() if (!isAdmin) forbidden() // render dashboard using session } ``` Because `getSession()` returns `role: 'user'`, visiting `/admin` should always hit the 403 path until that mock is changed. session_id: ses_007267adbffeCbgfBWZTYP8uv1
